accFilterValidation.caveat: This validation covers ONLY motion-induced artefacts. Electrode-contact problems produce RR junk WITHOUT an ACC spike (TN for ACC, yet an artefact in the RR) → that remains the job of the RR-only plausibility filter (Lipponen-Tarvainen 2019). Also: the validation targets themselves (FP<5%, Sens>70%) rest on OUR OWN conservative definition — they have not been demonstrated retrospectively on CARLON field data. (2026-08-14 citation audit: this used to read 'calibrated against the Stucke 2015 equine resting cohort'; Stucke 2015 is a methodological review and has no cohort at all — the calibration claim was unsupported.)
accFilterValidation.methodology: EquineACCArtifactCorrelator (snapshot taken at recording stop). For every beat removed by the RR pipeline (P0-3 Lipponen-Tarvainen), a ±300 ms window is checked for whether the Polar H10 ACC magnitude (200 Hz Z axis, z>2.0 vs EWMA baseline) shows a spike. ACC serves as an independent physical ground truth for 'was that a motion artefact?'. TP=correctly removed; FP=DANGER: real physiology cut away; FN=artefact slipped through; TN=correctly kept.
accFilterValidation.verdict: Filter-infrastructure ready; no ACC stream present in this session. Will populate automatically on first recording with active Polar H10 ACC stream.
accFilterValidation.verdictDE: Filter-Infrastruktur steht; in dieser Session keine ACC-Daten. Wird automatisch befüllt bei erster Aufnahme mit aktivem Polar H10 ACC-Stream.

interpretationCaveats: Equine-species-domain notice — human HRV norms do not apply. Equine resting RMSSD working range: 100–200 ms (CARLON own definition, no verified literature source). HUMAN healthy 30–50 ms is PATHOLOGICALLY LOW for a horse. Equine SDNN working range: 80–250 ms (own definition). Equine AFib-suspect RMSSD: >250 ms (NOT 150 ms which is human convention). Horses have much stronger vagal modulation + physiological AV-blocks → larger beat-to-beat variability.

EQUINE-ASTHMA REFERENCE — Nyerges-Bohák Z, Kovács L, Povázsai Á, Hamar E, Póti P, Ladányi M (2025), Equine Vet J 57(3):611–618, PMID 39275917, doi:10.1111/evj.14414: 20 horses with SEVERE equine asthma (sEA, BAL-confirmed) vs 20 respiratorily unremarkable controls (controls received NO BAL). Mean RMSSD 55.3 ± 19.8 ms (sEA) vs 86.0 ± 22.6 ms (controls). The study reports NO diagnostic cut-off, and its authors name SD2, SDNN, TINN and the SD2/SD1 ratio — NOT RMSSD — as the stronger discriminators. A former CARLON threshold 'RMSSD <95 ms suggests sEA' was WITHDRAWN 2026-08-14: it is not in the paper and would have sat above the healthy controls' own mean. Values 100–200 ms indicate normal vagal tone, NOT artifact contamination.

AV-block-label semantics: only the LONG pause-beat is labeled 'AVB'. The following short compensatory beat is 'LS' (long-short pair). This matches the physiological event — the AV-block IS the pause; the next beat is just the rhythm returning to baseline.
Vagal AV-block in trained horses is NORMAL — not pathological.
Equine HRV reference ranges are species-specific — DO NOT apply human Kubios baselines.
Single-session metrics need ≥5min stable resting epoch to be reliable.
Drug effects (beta-blockers, sedatives) dominate HRV signal — see subject.currentMedications.
Recent shoeing (<120 min) measurably alters HRV/Stress Index (Huangsaksri et al. 2024, PLoS One, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0305031) — note as confounder, not pathology.
observations: RMSSD 100.2ms is within the CARLON equine working band (100–200 ms; own definition, NOT a literature value). HUMAN ranges (30–50 ms) DO NOT apply to horses — strong vagal modulation + AV-blocks are physiological.
Baevsky Stress Index (normalized √SI) = 2.57. niedrig (relativ) · equine Referenz vorläufig.
⚠ Cross-validation flag: LF/HF differs 82% between Welch (PSD) and Lomb-Scargle methods. Cite LF/HF with explicit method qualifier; do not over-interpret the absolute value in this session.
recommendedNextSteps: All metrics within healthy reference ranges. Continue routine monitoring.

acuteColic.disclaimer: Acute indicator, NOT a diagnosis. The underlying studies were carried out on horses that already showed clinical signs on admission; the thresholds used here are derived from them, but are NOT published and have not been checked against any independent cohort. Known gap: conservatively treated colic horses in Gehlen 2020 had a mean LF/HF below the threshold used here. Veterinary examination is mandatory.
acuteColic.recommendation: If clinical signs are present (rolling, abdominal pain, apathy), contact a veterinary practice immediately. The indicator rests on HRV patterns of symptomatic colic horses — it is not an early warning in asymptomatic animals.

afibHint.cutoffReconciliation: 302 ms = heuristische, höher-spezifische Beobachtungs-Schwelle (angelehnt an Broux 2017/2018 — kein publizierter Fix-Cutoff). referenceRanges.afibSuspectRMSSDms.low = 150 ms is the generic Poincaré-cluster investigation threshold (high sensitivity, covers vagal AV-block bursts as well as early AFib). Both thresholds are correct for their respective observation tiers.
afibHint.disclaimer: AFib can occur in trained horses with high vagal tone without clinical relevance. The ~302 ms threshold is HEURISTIC (modelled on Broux 2017/2018 — not a published fixed cutoff), a pattern observation, NOT a diagnosis.
afibHint.recommendation: A standard ECG taken by a veterinary practice is recommended to differentiate AFib. AFib is the most common performance-limiting arrhythmia in the horse and responds well to treatment when found early.
sources: Broux et al. 2018 (BMC Vet Res, PMC6203204)

asthmaScreen.disclaimer: HONEST PROVENANCE (Sprint 11.6.46): Engine v2.4 was calibrated against the group statistics published in Nyerges-Bohák 2025 (EVJ DOI 10.1111/evj.14414) (mean±SD per marker per group). That study validates NO CARLON algorithm; it shows HRV differences in n=40 BAL-confirmed horses. CARLON validation: Monte-Carlo n=400 virtual patients drawn from the published distributions → Sens ~100% / Spec ~92% at HIGH-cut 3.5. A true LOO-CV on per-patient raw data is methodologically IMPOSSIBLE (raw RR series not public). Provenance code='c' (CARLON best config on simulated data). Secondary markers (LF/HF, HR) were non-significant in the study at p=0.13. The pNN50/RMSSD paradox marker is CARLON-novel, NOT covered by the study. Observation indicator, NOT a diagnosis. BAL remains the gold standard. | The verdict (triggered/severity) is derived from the V2 engine — ONE consistent asthma truth across app card, JSON and PDF (2026-07-09).
asthmaScreen.recommendation: Veterinary work-up with BALF (bronchoalveolar lavage) as the diagnostic gold standard is recommended.

crossValidation.differentiator: Each metric is reported with a paired second-method estimate (Welch vs Lomb-Scargle, RMSSD vs SD1×√2, SampEn vs MSE-scale-1) for internal consistency checking.

alternative.method: Lomb-Scargle periodogram on unequal-sampled RR (no interpolation)

lfHfRatio.interpretation: Lomb-Scargle avoids spline-interpolation bias. >15% divergence flags spectral analysis instability per Clifford 2002.

crossValidation.note: Self-verification: each main metric computed via two independent methods. Agreement <5% = methods cross-confirm; >15% = data instability flag. Standard in HRV methodology papers (Clifford 2002, Sassi 2015).

rmssdMs.interpretation: Methods agree to <1% — analytical identity confirmed.

alternative.referenceCitation: Costa, Goldberger & Peng 2002, Phys Rev Lett 89:068102

sampleEntropy.interpretation: Two independent implementations of the same Richman-Moorman algorithm. Discrepancy >5% flags numerical-stability issue (template-matching tolerance edge cases).

device.rrQuantisationNote: RR values from the H10 internal memory arrive as whole milliseconds: Polar's exercise protobuf carries `PbExerciseRRIntervals.rr_intervals` as `repeated uint32` in ms, so the device quantises before we ever see the data. The 1024 Hz figure above is the sensor's internal oscillator, NOT the resolution of this series. CARLON performs no rounding on this path (parser: EquineH10ExerciseParser). A BLE live-stream recording carries 1/1024 s steps (0.9765625 ms) and is exported by a different pipeline.

ecg_event_snippets_availability.clinical_consequence: AV-Block differentiation (vagal vs. Mobitz I vs. Mobitz II) cannot be confirmed from THIS export alone. For waveform-based differentiation use the Live-EKG export, or pair with a clinical ECG strip during a vet visit.
ecg_event_snippets_availability.how_to_obtain_snippets: Open the horse profile → Live-EKG → Start recording → Stop → Use 'Full Recording Export'. The resulting JSON includes µV waveform plus 10s snippets around each clinical event.
ecg_event_snippets_availability.reason: This export is from an RR-only recording (offline or HR-aggregated). The µV ECG waveform is only available during a Live-ECG-Stream session — that produces a separate 'carlon_equine_ecg_full_recording_v1_8_1' JSON which contains ecg_event_snippets.

integrity.verify: python3 -c "import json,hashlib; d=json.load(open('export.json')); rrs=[x['rrMs'] for x in d['rrData']]; s=','.join(f'{r:.2f}' for r in rrs); print(hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest())"

frequencyDomain.citation: Kuwahara M et al. (1996). Assessment of autonomic nervous function by power spectral analysis of HRV in the horse. J Auton Nerv Syst 60(1-2):43-48. PMID 8884694 — originates the equine LF 0.01-0.07 / HF 0.07-0.6 Hz bands. Relayed in Stucke D et al. (2015) Appl Anim Behav Sci 166:1-10 and von Borell E et al. (2007) Physiol Behav 92(3):293-316 (PMID 17320122), both methodological reviews.
frequencyDomain.methodology: Direct-DFT band-integration · Equine bands (origin: Kuwahara 1996; Stucke 2015 / von Borell 2007 only relay them) · variable bin-step (VLF 0.001 Hz, LF 0.002 Hz, HF 0.005 Hz) · Goertzel-style power-at-frequency on 4-Hz cubic-spline-resampled signal · Welch-segmented CI (256-sample windows, 50% overlap, Hamming) · bypasses legacy vDSP_fft_zripD SIGSEGV

lombScargle.methodology: Lomb-Scargle periodogram on raw (uninterpolated) RR timestamps — no 4-Hz cubic-spline interpolation bias
lombScargle.reference: Clifford 2002 MIT PhD; Lomb 1976; Scargle 1982. No equine-specific Lomb-Scargle reference could be verified (targeted search 2026-08-14 returned none); the method is species-agnostic.

mse.reference: Costa, Goldberger, Peng 2002 Phys Rev Lett 89:068102

nonLinear.cviLogBase: log10 (Toichi 1997 J Auton Nerv Syst 62:79–84 original)
nonLinear.dfaAlpha1ReliabilityNote: n=325 beats, no bootstrap CI available — DO NOT cite point estimate alone.

stationarityTest.method: ADF (lag-0, constant) AND an 8-block mean-shift test (<20 %). isStationary requires BOTH — ADF alone (H0 = unit root) reliably rejects on an exercise ramp even though the series is not mean-stationary.
stationarityTest.reference: Dickey & Fuller 1979 JASA; MacKinnon 1996 J Appl Econometrics; Block-Mean-Shift-Guard 2026-08-02

symbolicDynamics.reference: Porta 2001 IEEE Trans Biomed Eng; Guzzetti 2005 Circulation

timeDomain.disclosureGuide: RMSSD-triplet: raw=130.2ms (all beats incl. AVB+LS+ectopic) · headline=100.2ms (drop-pair: AVB+LS excluded, default vet display) · normalOnly=69.3ms (strict Lipponen-Tarvainen .normal only). Δ headline↔normalOnly = 31%. Δ >50% may indicate pipeline labeling aggressively excludes legitimate vagal Long-Short pairs (equine RSA-physiology). Inspect Poincaré clusters before clinical interpretation.
timeDomain.interpretation: RMSSD 100.2ms — innerhalb des CARLON-Arbeitsbereichs (100–200 ms; eigene Festlegung, kein Literaturwert) · SDNN 132.3ms — innerhalb des CARLON-Arbeitsbereichs (80–250 ms; eigene Festlegung, kein Literaturwert)

avBlockCount.note: Equine vagal AV-block is physiologically NORMAL in resting trained horses (van Loon 2019, Vet Clin North Am Equine Pract 35(1):85–102, PMID 30871832) — NOT pathology unless symptomatic. Differential vs Mobitz I/II requires ECG-strip.
avBlockCount.snomedCtLabel: Atrioventricular block (disorder) — equine-context: vagal AVB is normal in trained horses

dfaAlpha1.note: Detrended Fluctuation Analysis short-term scaling exponent (Peng 1995, window 4-16 beats). No LOINC code; cite Peng 1995 directly.

hfPowerMs2.loincLabel: Heart rate variability - high frequency power (HF)
hfPowerMs2.note: Equine HF band 0.07-0.6 Hz (Kuwahara M et al. 1996, J Auton Nerv Syst 60(1-2):43-48, PMID 8884694), differs from human 0.15-0.4 Hz.

lfHfRatio.note: Cite with explicit method qualifier (Welch vs Lomb-Scargle, see crossValidation.lfHfRatio).

lfPowerMs2.loincLabel: Heart rate variability - low frequency power (LF)
lfPowerMs2.note: Equine LF band 0.01-0.07 Hz (Kuwahara M et al. 1996, J Auton Nerv Syst 60(1-2):43-48, PMID 8884694), differs from human 0.04-0.15 Hz.

pNN50Pct.loincLabel: Heart rate variability - percentage of NN intervals differing >50ms (pNN50)

rmssdMs.loincLabel: Heart rate variability - root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD)
rmssdMs.note: LOINC 80394-6 is human-derived but widely used in equine HRV literature. Use FHIR R4 Observation with code.coding.system='http://loinc.org'.
rmssdMs.snomedCtLabel: Heart rate (observable entity) — HRV variability index

sampleEntropy.note: Sample Entropy (Richman-Moorman 2000) m=2, r=0.2·SDNN. No LOINC; cite Richman-Moorman directly.

sd1Ms.note: Poincaré-plot SD1 (Brennan 2001) — short-axis = √(½) × RMSSD identity. No LOINC code as of 2026-05; use vendor-specific extension.

sd2Ms.note: Poincaré-plot SD2 (Brennan 2001) — long-axis = √(2·SDNN² − ½·RMSSD²). No LOINC code as of 2026-05.

sdnnMs.loincLabel: Heart rate variability - standard deviation of NN intervals (SDNN)

indirectIdentifierRisk.rationale: Combination of 5 quasi-identifiers narrows identity to ≤3 horses in a typical regional database (Sweeney 2002 k-anonymity heuristic, adapted for equine populations). NOTE: this is an ESTIMATED re-identification floor against an ASSUMED regional reference population (Sweeney 2002 heuristic), not a measured k-anonymity of this single-record export — true k requires the release dataset.

anonymization.note: Explicit privacy-depth block per FAIR-A (Accessibility / Privacy). Helps researchers and owners assess re-identification risk BEFORE sharing. Standard in clinical data exports (HIPAA Safe Harbor + GDPR-Art.4.5 pseudonymisation), virtually absent in commercial HRV exports.

publicationRecommendations.note: Apply these transforms before public dataset release to raise k-anonymity ≥5. Removes direct IDs and broadens quasi-IDs into bins large enough to prevent unique identification.

privacy.gdprBasis: subject (animal) — research consent owner is researcher

humanRecordingConsent.note: Consent of a recorded PERSON (second chest strap in the coherence flow), confirmed in-app on this device before recording. Distinct from researchContribution.aggregationOptIn, which is about opting the dataset into research aggregation. Revocable in Settings; revoking also deletes the stored person name.

wasDerivedFrom.rawDataSource: H10 internal-flash RR recording · device delivers whole-millisecond RR (Polar PbExerciseRRIntervals.rr_intervals, repeated uint32); 1024 Hz is the sensor's internal oscillator, not the resolution of this series · no rounding applied by CARLON (see device.rrQuantisationNote)

usedAlgorithms.name: Welch-PSD

Die früher hier genannten Arbeiten (Stucke 2015, von Borell 2007, Ille 2014) sind Methoden-Reviews bzw. eine Geräte-Vergleichsstudie und enthalten keine equinen Referenzbereiche. · equin, NICHT human (Mensch 30–50 ms wäre für ein Pferd pathologisch)

healthyTriangularIndex.source: Task Force 1996 — human-derived; the extrapolation to the horse is ours

restingHRBpm.source: CARLON working range — conservative in-house definition, NOT a literature value. The 28–44 bpm figure is equine textbook common ground, but we have not verified it against a primary source and therefore do not attribute it to one.

stressedRMSSDms.source: CARLON own definition, NOT a literature value — below the working range (100–200 ms); <60 ms = markedly reduced. EQUINE pathologically low, NOT human-low

reliabilityReference.note: Change > MDC95 is statistically detectable at p<0.05
reliabilityReference.source: CARLON in-house assumption — ICC values are an internal working assumption, NOT a literature value. A targeted search (Europe PMC, CrossRef, web) for the previously cited 'van der Weide et al. 2021 (Utrecht)' returned no such publication. MDC95 below is therefore derived from an assumed, not a measured, reliability.

reproducibility.floatingPointMode: IEEE-754-double (Swift Double on arm64/x86_64) — Accelerate vDSP uses same FP semantics. NO denormal-as-zero flag. Reproducibility verified across iPhone 12-17 + macOS Intel/ARM (same byte-output for same input).
reproducibility.note: Re-running the same rrIntervalsMs through this build of the app produces a byte-identical export, EXCEPT for: schema.generated timestamp, provenance.wasGeneratedBy.startedAt/endedAt, and aggregationOptIn.consentTimestamp (if changed). Strip those three fields before computing a top-level reproducibility-hash. The integrity.rrDataSha256 alone is deterministic given the input.
reproducibility.rngAlgorithm: SplitMix64 (Vigna 2015) — passes BigCrush statistical test suite
reproducibility.seedRationale: Fixed seed (42) for SplitMix64 bootstrap-RNG. Choice is arbitrary but pinned — across reruns of the same rrIntervalsMs, sd1CI95/sd2CI95/dfaAlpha1CI95/sampleEntropyCI95 are byte-identical. Changing the seed shifts CI bounds by ~1-3% (sampling noise within the bootstrap-distribution itself), not the central values.

aggregationOptIn.note: Owner has NOT opted in to research aggregation. Default-off. To opt in, set in Settings > Privacy > Research-Contribution and re-export.

researchContribution.note: Research-Contribution = export-ready metadata for Open-Science aggregation. Opt-in is owner-controlled (default false). Fingerprint allows deduplication across re-exports without revealing PII. Aggregation targets are aspirational — opt-in does not auto-submit; it marks the session as eligible for the owner to manually contribute via the contactURL.

openHRVPlatform.description: Cross-species HRV reference platform (human + equine + canine) for comparative autonomic-nervous-system research.
openHRVPlatform.eligibility: Any session with cross-validation block present (this schema v1.7.1+), method-comparison metadata required.

vitalkulturEquineHRV2026.description: Open-source equine HRV reference database aggregating anonymized rest-session metrics across breeds, ages, and fitness levels — addresses the gap that published equine HRV cutoffs rest on very few small studies, and the most-cited works (Stucke 2015, von Borell 2007) are methodological reviews without reference ranges.
vitalkulturEquineHRV2026.eligibility: Any rest-session ≥5 min, anonymization required (subject.id stripped, only fingerprint hash retained), motion-context = rest or mixed.

respiratoryDualMethod.disclaimer: Respiratory-rate observation — not a diagnosis. The veterinary practice decides on clinical relevance. Dual-method divergence is an observation tool, not a verdict.
respiratoryDualMethod.interpretation: ACC weak (very quiet breathing or motion artifacts?) — relying on RSA-derived rate
limitations: No ACC snapshot for this session — only the RSA single method is available. Bridge-active recordings (offline recording path) provide ACC; the live-stream path (BLE-only) currently has no ACC channel.
methodology: ACC method: Polar H10 Z axis 50 Hz · band-pass 0.1-0.7 Hz · FFT peak → breathing movement of the horse's abdomen

RSA method: tachogram FFT in the HF band 0.07-0.4 Hz (equine HF band per Kuwahara et al. 1996, PMID 8884694; truncated at 0.4 Hz at the top here) → autonomic-vagal modulation of the heart rate with the breath
Cross-validator: 5-level divergence (excellent <3 BrPM Δ, minor 3-8, sympathetic_dominant ACC↑/RSA↓ >8, shallow_breathing RSA↑/ACC↓ >8, arrhythmia_suspect RSA fail at normal HR)
respiratoryDualMethod.validationReference: CARLON H10 dual-method consistency check 2026-06-27 (N=1, H10): ACC-derived respiratory rate 7.3 vs RSA-derived 7.3 BrPM, Δ=0.0 BrPM. A single measurement for methodological consistency — not a population validation.

sanityVerdict.rationale: The session is plausible and may be admitted into the dynamic_30d baseline.

preprocessing.artifactStrategy: Classified beats marked in rrData.label; non-finite values dropped before metrics; AV-blocks preserved (equine-physiological per van Loon 2019, Vet Clin North Am Equine Pract 35(1):85–102, PMID 30871832)
preprocessing.detrending: Tarvainen 2002 Smoothness-Priors (Accelerate-vDSP) on resampled signal before FFT
preprocessing.resampling: Cubic-spline interpolation at 4 Hz uniform grid (Task Force 1996 standard)

standardsApplied: Peng et al. 1995 (Detrended Fluctuation Analysis α1)

Stucke D, Große Ruse M, Lebelt D (2015). Measuring heart rate variability in horses — pros and cons of different methods. Appl Anim Behav Sci 166:1-10. doi:10.1016/j.applanim.2015.02.007 (methodological review)
von Borell E et al. (2007). HRV as a measure of autonomic regulation for assessing stress and welfare in farm animals — a review. Physiol Behav 92(3):293-316. PMID 17320122 (methodological review)
Kuwahara M et al. (1996). Assessment of autonomic nervous function by power spectral analysis of HRV in the horse. J Auton Nerv Syst 60(1-2):43-48. PMID 8884694 (equine LF/HF band definition)
van Loon G. (2019). Cardiac arrhythmias in horses. Vet Clin North Am Equine Pract 35(1):85–102. PMID 30871832 (equine AV-block classification)
